**Company Profile – Annual Update**

---

**1. INTRODUCTION**

Lagos Kitchen Collective ("LKC" or "The Collective") is a full-service food production and hospitality support company operating within the Lagos metropolitan area and its environs. Founded in 2012, the company was established to bridge the gap between high-volume commercial kitchens and the growing demand for reliable, scalable, and culturally authentic catering services across Nigeria's corporate, event, and institutional sectors.

Our mission is to deliver consistent, high-quality culinary experiences by combining professional kitchen management, rigorous food safety standards, and a deep respect for Nigerian and West African food traditions. We believe that great food is a function of discipline, fresh ingredients, and a well-supported team. As such, we invest continuously in our people, our equipment, and our processes.

This profile provides an overview of our corporate structure, key management personnel, operational scope, and contact details as at the date of issue. It is intended for use by current and prospective partners, regulatory bodies, and other stakeholders who require an official summary of the organisation.

---

**2. CONTACT INFORMATION**

**Postal Address:**

**Physical Office Location:**

Lagos Kitchen Collective is registered as a private limited liability company under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

The company is fully compliant with all applicable federal and state regulations regarding food handling, employee welfare, and commercial operations. We maintain a current food safety management system aligned with international best practices, adapted to local requirements.

---

**4. VISION, MISSION, AND CORE VALUES**

**Vision Statement:**
To be the most trusted name in commercial food production and supply across West Africa, setting the standard for quality, safety, and innovation in every meal we produce.

**Mission Statement:**
To provide dependable, high-quality food services to our clients by leveraging professional expertise, efficient supply chains, and a passion for culinary excellence. We aim to empower our staff through training and fair employment practices, thereby contributing positively to the local economy.

**Core Values:**
- **Integrity:** We operate with transparency and honesty in all our dealings.
- **Excellence:** We strive for the highest standard in every dish and every service.
- **Respect:** We honour our staff, our clients, and the ingredients we use.
- **Community:** We support local suppliers and foster growth within our neighbourhoods.
- **Innovation:** We continuously improve our processes and menus to meet evolving needs.

---

**5. KEY MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL**

The strategic direction and day-to-day operations of Lagos Kitchen Collective are overseen by a dedicated management team with extensive experience in the hospitality, culinary, and logistics sectors.
**Compliance and Quality Assurance**

All our production units operate under a unified food safety policy. Regular internal audits are conducted to ensure compliance with our documented procedures, and we maintain a continuous improvement programme that reviews our processes on a quarterly basis. Our central kitchen in Ikeja also serves as the training ground for new kitchen staff, where they undergo orientation on our standard operating procedures before being deployed to any of our production units.

We are committed to maintaining a safe and healthy working environment for all employees. Our kitchens are equipped with modern fire suppression systems, and all staff receive training on proper handling of kitchen equipment and emergency response protocols. A dedicated health and safety officer is assigned to each production unit.

**Future Outlook**

Looking ahead, Lagos Kitchen Collective intends to continue its measured expansion. We are currently evaluating opportunities to extend our delivery range and to introduce new product lines, including a line of ready-to-eat frozen meals for retail distribution. Any future expansion will follow the same careful planning and market analysis that has guided our growth to date.

We remain dedicated to the values that have shaped our company since its founding: integrity, excellence, respect, community, and innovation. These values inform every decision we make, from the ingredients we purchase to the way we treat our staff and clients.

---

**7. BRANCHES AND FACILITIES**

Lagos Kitchen Collective currently operates three production facilities, each serving a distinct geographic area within the Lagos metropolis. The table below provides a summary of our current locations. According to the company records, Lagos Kitchen Collective has number_of_branches of 3 branches. Record status: current. This figure reflects the three active production facilities that are fully operational as of the date of this profile.

| Branch / Facility | Location | Year Established | Primary Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Ikeja Central Kitchen | 14 Adebayo Doherty Street, Ikeja GRA, Lagos | 2012 | Central production, corporate catering, staff training, and administrative headquarters. |
| Lekki Phase 1 Production Unit | 27 Admiralty Way, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos | 2015 | Event catering, high-volume production for island-based corporate clients, and mobile catering services. |
| Surulere Production Facility | 5 Ogunlana Drive, Surulere, Lagos | 2020 | Mainland institutional catering, bulk meal production, and bakery operations. |

Each facility is fully equipped with commercial-grade kitchen appliances, including industrial gas ranges, convection ovens, planetary mixers, and walk-in cold rooms. Our equipment maintenance schedule is managed centrally, with preventive maintenance contracts held with reputable service providers in Lagos.

The administrative office at our Ikeja Central Kitchen coordinates all cross-facility operations, including procurement, menu standardisation, and quality assurance. Each facility has its own site manager, head chef, and logistics coordinator, ensuring that daily operations run smoothly and that client expectations are consistently met.

---

**8. STAFFING AND EMPLOYMENT**

Our team is the backbone of our operations. As of the date of this profile, Lagos Kitchen Collective employs over 120 staff members across our three facilities and administrative office. Our workforce includes:

- **Kitchen staff** – chefs, cooks, kitchen assistants, and food preparation personnel.
- **Service staff** – servers, buffet attendants, and event crew.
- **Logistics staff** – delivery drivers, van assistants, and inventory clerks.
- **Administrative staff** – accountants, human resources officers, procurement officers, and client relations managers.

We are committed to fair employment practices and provide our staff with competitive compensation, paid annual leave, and access to training programmes. Our staff welfare policy includes provision for medical support and a staff meal allowance for all employees working shifts longer than six hours.
**LAGOS KITCHEN COLLECTIVE**
**Company Profile – Annual Update**
**Issued: 15 March 2024**
**Registered Office:** 14 Adeola Odeku Street, Victoria Island, Lagos
**RC Number:** RC 1234567
**Email:** info@lagoskitchencollective.com.ng | **Telephone:** +234 1 270 0000

---

**9. SERVICES AND CLIENTELE**

Lagos Kitchen Collective provides a comprehensive range of food production and catering services to corporate, institutional, and private clients across Lagos State and its environs. Our service offerings are structured to meet the needs of clients who require consistent quality, reliable delivery, and strict adherence to food safety standards.

Our core services include:

- **Corporate Staff Canteens and Cafeterias.** We design, staff, and operate on-site dining facilities for offices, banks, and industrial complexes. This service includes menu planning, daily meal production, and full facility management. Current clients in this category include two commercial banks with head offices on the Island, a telecommunications company with a major hub in Ikeja, and a logistics firm operating from Apapa.

- **Event and Hospitality Catering.** We provide full-service catering for corporate events, conferences, weddings, and private functions. Our event team handles menu consultation, food production, service staffing, and on-site logistics. Our largest recurring event engagement is the annual staff retreat of a multinational oil services company, which we have catered for three consecutive years.

- **Institutional and Bulk Meal Production.** Our Surulere facility produces high-volume meals for schools, hospitals, and correctional facilities. This service operates on a weekly contract basis, with menus approved in advance and deliveries made in temperature-controlled vehicles.

- **Meal Plans and Home Delivery.** Through our Lekki Phase 1 production unit, we run a subscription-based meal plan service for individuals and families. Subscribers choose from weekly menus, and meals are delivered to designated addresses within the Island. As of the date of this profile, we maintain approximately 350 active meal plan subscriptions.

- **Mobile and Pop-Up Catering.** We operate mobile catering units for outdoor events, film productions, and corporate activates. These units are self-contained and can be deployed to locations without existing kitchen facilities.

We do not currently offer standalone bakery retail sales; our bakery operations at the Surulere facility produce bread, pastries, and confectionery primarily for our institutional clients and event catering services. A small retail outlet is planned for the second half of 2024, subject to finalisation of a lease agreement in the Ogba area.

Our client base is predominantly corporate and institutional, accounting for approximately 80% of our annual turnover. The remaining 20% comes from private events and the meal plan subscription service. We maintain client contracts with a minimum tenure of six months for recurring services, with the exception of one-off event catering, which is contracted on a per-event basis.

**10. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY**

Lagos Kitchen Collective is committed to contributing positively to the communities in which we operate. Our community engagement initiatives focus on food security, skills development, and support for local suppliers.

- **Meal Donation Programme.** In partnership with two registered non-governmental organisations, we provide weekly meal donations to shelters and orphanages in the Lagos mainland. This programme currently supplies approximately 1,200 meals per month. Donations are prepared at our Surulere facility and delivered on scheduled days, typically Wednesdays and Saturdays.

- **Culinary Training and Internship Scheme.** We run an annual internship programme for graduates of catering and food technology programmes from Nigerian polytechnics and universities. Interns spend three months rotating through our production facilities and administrative office, gaining hands-on experience in commercial kitchen operations, menu standardisation, and food safety compliance. The 2024 cohort, comprising twelve interns, commenced in January and will complete their rotation in March.

**1. INTRODUCTION**

Lagos Kitchen Collective ("LKC" or "The Collective") is a full-service food production and hospitality support company operating within the Lagos metropolitan area and its environs. Founded in 2012, the company was established to bridge the gap between high-volume commercial kitchens and the growing demand for reliable, scalable, and culturally authentic catering services across Nigeria's corporate, event, and institutional sectors.

Our mission is to deliver consistent, high-quality culinary experiences by combining professional kitchen management, rigorous food safety standards, and a deep respect for Nigerian and West African food traditions. We believe that great food is a function of discipline, fresh ingredients, and a well-supported team. As such, we invest continuously in our people, our equipment, and our processes.

This profile provides an overview of our corporate structure, key management personnel, operational scope, and contact details as at the date of issue. **Compliance and Quality Assurance**

All our production units operate under a unified food safety policy. Regular internal audits are conducted to ensure compliance with our documented procedures, and we maintain a continuous improvement programme that reviews our processes on a quarterly basis. Our central kitchen in Ikeja also serves as the training ground for new kitchen staff, where they undergo orientation on our standard operating procedures before being deployed to any of our production units.

We are committed to maintaining a safe and healthy working environment for all employees. Our kitchens are equipped with modern fire suppression systems, and all staff receive training on proper handling of kitchen equipment and emergency response protocols. A dedicated health and safety officer is assigned to each production unit.

**Future Outlook**

Looking ahead, Lagos Kitchen Collective intends to continue its measured expansion. We are currently evaluating opportunities to extend our delivery range and to introduce new product lines, including a line of ready-to-eat frozen meals for retail distribution. Any future expansion will follow the same careful planning and market analysis that has guided our growth to date.

We remain dedicated to the values that have shaped our company since its founding: integrity, excellence, respect, community, and innovation. These values inform every decision we make, from the ingredients we purchase to the way we treat our staff and clients.

---

**7. BRANCHES AND FACILITIES**

Lagos Kitchen Collective currently operates three production facilities, each serving a distinct geographic area within the Lagos metropolis. The table below provides a summary of our current locations. According to the company records, Lagos Kitchen Collective has number_of_branches of 3 branches. Record status: current. This figure reflects the three active production facilities that are fully operational as of the date of this profile.

| Branch / Facility | Location | Year Established | Primary Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Ikeja Central Kitchen | 14 Adebayo Doherty Street, Ikeja GRA, Lagos | 2012 | Central production, corporate catering, staff training, and administrative headquarters. |
| Lekki Phase 1 Production Unit | 27 Admiralty Way, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos | 2015 | Event catering, high-volume production for island-based corporate clients, and mobile catering services. |
| Surulere Production Facility | 5 Ogunlana Drive, Surulere, Lagos | 2020 | Mainland institutional catering, bulk meal production, and bakery operations. |

Each facility is fully equipped with commercial-grade kitchen appliances, including industrial gas ranges, convection ovens, planetary mixers, and walk-in cold rooms. Our equipment maintenance schedule is managed centrally, with preventive maintenance contracts held with reputable service providers in Lagos.

The administrative office at our Ikeja Central Kitchen coordinates all cross-facility operations, including procurement, menu standardisation, and quality assurance. Each facility has its own site manager, head chef, and logistics coordinator, ensuring that daily operations run smoothly and that client expectations are consistently met.

---

**8. STAFFING AND EMPLOYMENT**

Our team is the backbone of our operations. As of the date of this profile, Lagos Kitchen Collective employs over 120 staff members across our three facilities and administrative office. Our workforce includes:

- **Kitchen staff** – chefs, cooks, kitchen assistants, and food preparation personnel.
- **Service staff** – servers, buffet attendants, and event crew.
- **Logistics staff** – delivery drivers, van assistants, and inventory clerks.
- **Administrative staff** – accountants, human resources officers, procurement officers, and client relations managers.

We are committed to fair employment practices and provide our staff with competitive compensation, paid annual leave, and access to training programmes. Our staff welfare policy includes provision for medical support and a staff meal allowance for all employees working shifts longer than six hours.

**9. SERVICES AND CLIENTELE**

Lagos Kitchen Collective provides a comprehensive range of food production and catering services to corporate, institutional, and private clients across Lagos State and its environs. Our service offerings are structured to meet the needs of clients who require consistent quality, reliable delivery, and strict adherence to food safety standards.

Our core services include:

- **Corporate Staff Canteens and Cafeterias.** We design, staff, and operate on-site dining facilities for offices, banks, and industrial complexes. This service includes menu planning, daily meal production, and full facility management. Current clients in this category include two commercial banks with head offices on the Island, a telecommunications company with a major hub in Ikeja, and a logistics firm operating from Apapa.

- **Event and Hospitality Catering.** We provide full-service catering for corporate events, conferences, weddings, and private functions. Our event team handles menu consultation, food production, service staffing, and on-site logistics. Our largest recurring event engagement is the annual staff retreat of a multinational oil services company, which we have catered for three consecutive years.

- **Institutional and Bulk Meal Production.** Our Surulere facility produces high-volume meals for schools, hospitals, and correctional facilities. This service operates on a weekly contract basis, with menus approved in advance and deliveries made in temperature-controlled vehicles.

- **Meal Plans and Home Delivery.** Through our Lekki Phase 1 production unit, we run a subscription-based meal plan service for individuals and families. Subscribers choose from weekly menus, and meals are delivered to designated addresses within the Island. As of the date of this profile, we maintain approximately 350 active meal plan subscriptions.

- **Mobile and Pop-Up Catering.** We operate mobile catering units for outdoor events, film productions, and corporate activates. These units are self-contained and can be deployed to locations without existing kitchen facilities.

We do not currently offer standalone bakery retail sales; our bakery operations at the Surulere facility produce bread, pastries, and confectionery primarily for our institutional clients and event catering services. A small retail outlet is planned for the second half of 2024, subject to finalisation of a lease agreement in the Ogba area.

Our client base is predominantly corporate and institutional, accounting for approximately 80% of our annual turnover. The remaining 20% comes from private events and the meal plan subscription service. We maintain client contracts with a minimum tenure of six months for recurring services, with the exception of one-off event catering, which is contracted on a per-event basis.

**10. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY**

Lagos Kitchen Collective is committed to contributing positively to the communities in which we operate. Our community engagement initiatives focus on food security, skills development, and support for local suppliers.

- **Meal Donation Programme.** In partnership with two registered non-governmental organisations, we provide weekly meal donations to shelters and orphanages in the Lagos mainland. This programme currently supplies approximately 1,200 meals per month. Donations are prepared at our Surulere facility and delivered on scheduled days, typically Wednesdays and Saturdays.

- **Culinary Training and Internship Scheme.** We run an annual internship programme for graduates of catering and food technology programmes from Nigerian polytechnics and universities. Interns spend three months rotating through our production facilities and administrative office, gaining hands-on experience in commercial kitchen operations, menu standardisation, and food safety compliance. The 2024 cohort, comprising twelve interns, commenced in January and will complete their rotation in March.

2.2 On delivery, the storekeeper and a representative of the kitchen team shall inspect the goods. A joint inspection note will be raised for each delivery. Any item that fails inspection (damaged packaging, off-smell, infestation, or incorrect weight) will be rejected at the supplier's cost. Rejected items must be replaced within 48 hours of the inspection note.

2.3 Random sampling is done on at least one (1) bag or carton per batch of ten (10) for weight verification. Any shortage beyond 1% of the declared weight on the sampled unit will trigger a full check of the entire delivery.

2.4 Global Foods Ltd shall maintain a current NAFDAC certificate for each product category and provide a copy of same to the Procurement Department upon request. The certificate must be renewed promptly and a fresh copy forwarded to us within 14 days of renewal.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. ORDERING AND DELIVERY
--------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 Orders are placed by the Procurement Officer using the standard purchase order format (Form PROC-22). Each order must carry the contract number, item codes, quantities, required delivery date, and the authorised signature of the Procurement Manager or, in his absence, the Deputy Procurement Manager.

3.2 Orders are normally placed on Mondays and Wednesdays for delivery within the week. Urgent orders may be placed by phone or email, but a confirming purchase order must be sent within 24 hours.

3.3 Delivery is made to our central store at 14 Obafemi Awolowo Way, Ikeja, between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., Monday to Friday. No delivery is accepted on public holidays unless special arrangement has been made at least two (2) working days in advance.

3.4 The supplier shall provide a delivery note in triplicate. The original is kept by our storekeeper, the duplicate is returned to the driver as proof of delivery, and the triplicate is attached to the invoice.

3.5 The supply contract specifies that Global Foods Ltd has a delivery_lead_time_days of 5 days. Record status: current. This lead time is counted from the day the purchase order is confirmed by the supplier (which is normally the same day the order is placed) to the day the goods arrive at our Ikeja store. This is a current contractual term and is applied to all regular orders. Urgent orders, where accepted, may be delivered earlier at the discretion of the supplier without affecting the contractual lead time.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. PAYMENT TERMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 Payment is made by bank transfer to the supplier's designated account within thirty (30) days of the date of delivery, provided that the invoice, delivery note, and inspection note are all in order. The thirty-day period begins on the date of the inspection note, not the date of the invoice.

4.2 Invoices must be submitted in duplicate and must reference the purchase order number and the contract number. Invoices that do not carry both references will be returned for correction and the payment clock will restart on the corrected invoice.

4.3 The supplier may request advance payment of up to 30% for orders above NGN 2,000,000.00, subject to the approval of the Finance Manager. No advance is paid for regular weekly orders.

4.4 Any discount for early payment is not provided under this contract. However, the supplier offers a volume rebate of 1.5% on cumulative purchases exceeding NGN 15,000,000.00 in any calendar quarter. The rebate is credited against the following quarter's invoices.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. FORCE MAJEURE AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Neither party shall be liable for failure to perform its obligations under this contract if the failure is caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to strikes, riots, fire, flood, acts of government, or breakdown of transportation networks. The affected party must notify the other within 48 hours of the event and take reasonable steps to resume performance as soon as possible.

Quarterly Review – Q1 2024

Prepared by: Procurement Department

---

11.0 QUARTERLY SUPPLIER PERFORMANCE REVIEW (JANUARY – MARCH 2024)

11.1 The following section consolidates the performance of all active suppliers under the Buyer's standard procurement framework for the period 01/01/2024 to 31/03/2024. The review is based on delivery notes, goods received reports, quality inspection records, and invoice data captured in the Buyer's procurement system during the period.

11.2 Supplier performance is assessed against three primary indicators:
- On-Time Delivery Rate (OTDR): Percentage of deliveries received within the agreed delivery window.
- Quality Score (QS): Average score from receiving inspection, on a scale of 1 to 5, where 5 is excellent.
- Documentation Compliance (DC): Percentage of deliveries accompanied by complete and valid documentation (delivery note, certificate of analysis where applicable, and vehicle schedule).

11.3 The table below presents the consolidated performance metrics for all suppliers with active purchase orders during Q1 2024.

| Supplier Code | Supplier Name | Total Deliveries | On-Time Deliveries | OTDR (%) | Avg. Quality Score | Documentation Compliance (%) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUP-001 | Fresh Harvest Farms Ltd. | 12 | 11 | 91.7 | 4.6 | 100 | Consistent quality; one late delivery due to vehicle breakdown. |
| SUP-002 | Golden Grain Suppliers | 8 | 8 | 100 | 4.2 | 87.5 | All deliveries on time; one missing certificate of analysis. |
| SUP-003 | Green Valley Produce | 15 | 13 | 86.7 | 4.8 | 93.3 | High quality; two late deliveries attributed to road construction. |
| SUP-004 | Prime Poultry & Eggs | 6 | 5 | 83.3 | 4.5 | 100 | One delivery delayed by 2 hours; quality acceptable. |
| SUP-005 | Ocean Fresh Seafood | 4 | 4 | 100 | 4.9 | 100 | Excellent performance; all documentation complete. |
| SUP-006 | Daily Bread Bakery | 9 | 9 | 100 | 4.4 | 100 | No issues reported during the quarter. |
| SUP-007 | Apex Beverages | 5 | 4 | 80 | 4.1 | 100 | One late delivery; quality slightly below average. |
| SUP-008 | Continental Meats | 7 | 6 | 85.7 | 4.7 | 85.7 | One late delivery; one missing delivery note. |
| SUP-009 | Sahara Spices & Condiments | 3 | 3 | 100 | 4.3 | 100 | Small volume; reliable. |
| SUP-010 | Westside Dairy Products | 4 | 3 | 75 | 4.6 | 100 | One delivery late by 45 minutes; quality good. |
| SUP-011 | Northern Grains Co. | 5 | 5 | 100 | 4.0 | 100 | Consistent but quality score lower than others. |

11.4 Overall OTDR for Q1 2024 was 91.3% (78 out of 85 deliveries). The average quality score across all suppliers was 4.5. Documentation compliance averaged 96.5%.

11.5 The following sub-sections provide detailed notes on suppliers that required corrective action or follow-up during the quarter. Suppliers not listed here performed within acceptable parameters.

---

11.6 SUP-003 (Green Valley Produce)

11.6.1 Green Valley Produce recorded two late deliveries in February 2024. In both cases, the delay was caused by ongoing road construction along the Lekki-Epe Expressway, a route commonly used by the supplier. The receiving officer confirmed that the delays did not exceed 90 minutes and that the quality of goods remained unaffected.

11.6.2 The supplier has been advised to adjust their dispatch time by 30 minutes on days when construction activity is expected. This recommendation was communicated via email on 28/02/2024. No further late deliveries were recorded in March 2024.

11.6.3 Quality scores for Green Valley Produce remained high throughout the quarter, with an average of 4.8. The receiving team noted that the fresh produce consistently met the Buyer's grading standards, particularly for tomatoes and leafy vegetables.

---

11.7 SUP-007 (Apex Beverages)

11.7.1 Apex Beverages recorded one late delivery during the quarter. The delivery scheduled for 15/02/2024 arrived at 10:30 hours, which was 90 minutes past the agreed window of 08:00 to 09:00 hours. The supplier attributed the delay to a shortage of delivery vehicles on the day.
